title: Fork and Torte
subtitle: Lengthy procedures, excessive paperwork, and bureaucratic red tape.

trails.title: Employee Notes
trails.description: A crucial transcription, meticulously transcribed in bold for emphasis.

content.text: St. Pavlov Foundation Vienna Branch Employee Notes

Procedure for Requesting the Dispelling of a Mute Incantation (Simplified Version)

1. Initiating the Application

The applicant must go to the administrative desk of the St. Pavlov Foundation, Vienna Branch - Austro-Hungarian Empire Internal Security Department - Austro-Hungarian Empire Public Security Bureau with a ticket to receive the Joint Processing Application Form.

2. Filling Out the Form

The applicant must fill out the application form truthfully and submit it to the administrative desk of the Austro-Hungarian Empire Public Security Bureau, where the administrative staff will conduct a preliminary review.

3. Commencement of the Dispelling Procedure

After the administrative staff has conducted a preliminary review, the form will be submitted to the Social Responsibility Monitoring Group of the St. Pavlov Foundation, Vienna Branch - Austro-Hungarian Empire Internal Security Department - Austro-Hungarian Empire Public Security Bureau for risk assessment.

4. Commencement of the Assessment

Members of the Social Responsibility Monitoring Group will conduct a detailed investigation and assessment of the applicant, fill out their review comments, and submit them to the team leader.

5. Secondary Approval

The team leader will then summarize the review comments and submit them to the director of the Public Affairs Bureau for a secondary approval, who will then submit the application to the Internal Affairs Department.

6. Completion of the Process

Upon approval, the director of the Public Affairs Bureau will initiate an interdepartmental collaboration process and send the comments of the secondary approval to the Harm Prevention Office, which will then issue a notification letter to the administrative desk.

7. Execution of the Dispel

Upon receipt of the notification letter, the administrative desk will archive it and issue another notification letter informing the applicant to participate in the mute incantation dispel ritual.

Don't forget any of the steps or you'll regret it! This is my third @#&* time starting over! D**n it all. I don't ever want to fill out these d**n forms again!

items.text: Fork and Torte
Ring Road

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Here it is ... the national treasure of Austria!

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: The creamy chocolate cake, the buttery ganache, and the delicious apricot jam ...

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Created by the ingenious apprentice Franz Sacher in 1832, renowned throughout the world ... the dessert of Vienna, Sachertorte!

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: My first time seeing a real one.
At the café's entrance, Marcus's fork holds reluctantly over her mentor's little gift.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: How should I cut it?

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: If I cut straight, the cake will get mushy. If I cut sideways, I'll miss out on the apricot filling ...

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: What if I eat it in one bite ... No no, how unrefined. The director would scold me for that.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: I have to think carefully. There must be some other way ...

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Remember all your training, Investigator Marcus. This is the most important moment of your life! Don't get too excited or you'll ruin it!
Then the fork falls.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Oh, no!
As Hofmann cuts the Sachertorte in two with calculated precision.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: What?

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: No, nothing ... Thank you for deciding for me ...
The cake rightly is a national treasure, soft and layered with apricot jam. It is consumed in mere moments.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: *sobs*

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: What's with the tears, Marcus?

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Because ...

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: The cake ... is way too sweet ...
The café bustles with others coming and going.
As Hofmann checks her watch now for perhaps the fifteenth time in fewer than as many minutes.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: According to the plan, the head of the Vienna branch would pick us up and guide us through the necessary procedures of this era.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: But our train was two hours late.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: That being the case, our Mr. Karl should have been waiting for two hours, but so far there's no sign of any gentleman in the Foundation's uniform ...

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: So Mr. Karl is also more than two hours late.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: A clever deduction. Let us hope otherwise.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: I'll go check if he got here before us.
The mentor steps out from under her umbrella's shadow and heads into the café. Left behind, the apprentice looks around aimlessly.
She catches a few key words.

items.speaker: Passerby I
items.text: I bet that island is a secret base of the Dual Entente. That's why the Bulgarians are so anxious. They're worried about their exit on the Aegean Sea ...

items.speaker: Passerby I
items.text: A friend of mine is in the navy. He saw a ship leaving the harbor loaded with gold ...

items.speaker: Passerby I
items.text: War is coming, friend!

items.speaker: Passerby II
items.text: No, no! How does that explain the arcane creatures over there?

items.speaker: Passerby II
items.text: I'd say it's never been discovered before, like the Celtic Otherworld, you know, the heavenly land beyond the sea in Bran's legend.

items.speaker: Passerby II
items.text: The Arcanum has declined after the Enlightenment. It is an honor for all of us in this era to find such a paradise from the past.

items.speaker: Passerby II
items.text: You're not fit to be human if you don't understand what that island means to us, my friend!

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Secret base ... Otherworld ...

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Fascinating. I need to write this down.
Marcus opens her notebook, jotting down these bits of trivia with a quick and earnest enthusiasm.
Her desire to catch the length and breadth of these comments forces her to lean quite conspicuously until she finds she has become an object of spectacle herself.

items.speaker: Vienna Guard
items.text: Miss, could you show me your papers please?

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Ah, right.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: ... Erm, sorry. My friend has it. Could you hold on a minute?

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: I am an arcanist sent from the headquarters of the St. Pavlov Foundation. I have a letter of introduction from the head of the Vienna branch ...

items.speaker: Vienna Guard
items.text: Arcanist?

items.speaker: Vienna Guard
items.text: Then you come with us, miss! Hands up, and be quiet!

items.speaker: Vienna Guard
items.text: Bring over the golems! We have an unregistered arcanist!

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Huh? Huh?!
Hofmann's attention is drawn to the commotion unfolding outside the window.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: Marcus ...?!

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Sir? P-Please listen to me ...
A single misstep causes a mistaken interpretation—a sign of defiance.
Enough to compel these loyal city guardians to fulfill their duty.

items.speaker: Vienna Guard
items.text: Don't let her get away!
What is happening?
At ease, gents! Allow me to explain. This respectable lady is most definitely not a Russian spy!
A portly gentleman with a handlebar mustache hurries over, his forehead glistening with sweat.
Ah, Ms. Hofmann. So this lady with the big case is your ... assistant?
No spy would be stupid enough to carry an entire case of papers in public. That will be all, gentlemen!
The guards offer their salute before ushering the golems back to their posts.
Hofmann's face is the picture of awkwardness—one that could mark a new entry for this exact situation in the next Field Mission Manual.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: The gentlemen in Vienna have become exceedingly sensitive after the infamous espionage cases of 1913.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: And their pride was almost destroyed by the Redl case ... The man was even head of counterintelligence, and had a sexual orientation not tolerated in his time. Well, I'm not sure which of the reasons hurt them more.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: Sorry, Marcus. I should have told you that, as your supervisor.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Mmm ...
She nods but only manages a half-spoken grunt of affirmation.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: Hmm, the belief that arcanists cannot cast arcane skills without the ability to speak, so old and superstitious. Like muzzling a dog when it gets out of control.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: Can we dispel it now, Mr. Karl?

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: I have to remind you, Ms. Hofmann, that theoretically we have to go through an entire approval process before I authorize the dispelling of the mute spell.

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: But whatever, who cares! They shouldn't have treated a young lady like that, for whatever reason.
Mr. Karl is a portly and pale man, his appearance punctuated by the scent of punch cards, in every way a representative of the empire's bureaucratic system.
Overall, he seems a pleasant sort of man, despite his position.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: ... Phew!

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: Relax! This was just a minor incident! You'll never find another place as tolerant as Vienna—the very same principles the Foundation strives for!

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: All registered arcanists can come and go as they please in this beautiful city! We even offer artists and musicians perks that cover every aspect of their lives, because Vienna loves art and music!

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: Oh, speaking of registered arcanists ... Could you show me her arcanum license?

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: Arcanum license?

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: Yes, ladies from the headquarters! Even though I'm more than willing to skip some ... unnecessary procedures for you, we still have to be careful about security, you know, especially when dealing with arcanists.
The portly bureaucrat rubs his hands together slyly. It is evident that he would be no easier to deal with than the golems.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: I don't think the headquarters issues such a license. No one told us to apply for one.

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: Oh, there must be some mistake! All arcanists entering Europe must possess an arcanum license issued by the local government.

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: Austria enacted this policy in 1756. We abolished it in 1868, but we're in the time of great tension, so ... you know.

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: Perhaps this lady knows something ... Ms. Marcus?

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: ... Y-Yes?

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: You are an arcanist, even though you're sent by the headquarters, correct? Show it to me then, your arcanum license.
Hofmann's brow furrows. This then is what it looks like when those in power wish to exert their authority.
But the more pressing crisis here is that there would be no way to produce an authentic paper from 1914 without adequate preparation.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: Marcus is my assistant on this mission, Mr. Karl. She is not to answer your questions directly, given her rank and status.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: It is me, the one in charge, that you should turn to, not my assistant.

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: Oh, lady from headquarters, don't get me wrong. I didn't mean to usurp your authority! It's not an issue. You didn't have to ...

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: I-I have it!
Marcus hands over a slip of paper from her pocket.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Here.

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: Oh ... Huh!
Mr. Karl bursts into a series of protracted sighs.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Erm, is everything ok, Mr. Karl? Is it not acceptable ...?

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: Oh yes, it's a perfectly good license. I can even smell the ink from the government office! Welcome to Vienna, Ms. Arcanist from Romania!

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: You should have shown it to me sooner. It would have saved us a lot of trouble.
The portly man smiles as he returns the permit to Marcus, who seems as though she has just stepped off a rocking boat.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Erm, I'm so sorry to have wasted your time ...

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: Speaking of which, no offense, but you are two hours and fifteen minutes late, Mr. Karl.
The apprentice's apology is cut short, as she is taken aback by her mentor's dramatic shift in tact.

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: My apologies. The Minister of Finance and I had a little too much at lunch. Well, your train was late, too, wasn't it?

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: You were having lunch when you were supposed to be here? We agreed to ...

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: Relax, lady from the headquarters! You're just not used to the pace around here.

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: Look at this industrialization and so-called modern designs. They have turned our beloved city and our carefree life into a cold, impersonal machine.

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: Please forgive the train staff, the sewer workers, and the plumbers! It is their right to be a little "unpunctual," and enforcing this right is a symbol of our free will ...

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: In the end, you didn't wait too long, and I got to enjoy my lunch. It all worked out, right?
Hofmann remains unswayed and indignant, while behind her Marcus hangs her head.
Clearly, Mr. Karl's joy is his alone.

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: So, why was your train late?

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: It crashed into a deer, a deer with free will.

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: Oh. Tragic.

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: Alright. Forgive this old Karl for his minor mistake, ladies. The rumors about the Golden Isle had kept the branch busy. There was no one else but me to pick you up.

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: It wouldn't have been so embarrassing if headquarters had sent us manpower instead of taking it from us.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: I'm also on the job, Mr. Karl. Should I include your complaints in the report?

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: No no no, that's okay.

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: It's just a group of lunatics banished to an island. They are arcane criminals from a small country, and people will forget about them in less than a month.

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: Only a few would believe that it has any real influence on Vienna, you know, the young artists who think highly of themselves, the schemers with evil plans, and the conspiracy theorists suffering from neurasthenia.

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: The Magyars and the Bohemians are already giving us a headache ... Arcanists? They are not at all the Empire's top ethnic concern!

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: But aren't you in charge of the registration and management of arcanists?

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: Well, first of all, isn't my loyalty to His Majesty and the Empire?

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: Before you use the title, "Head of the Vienna Branch," to define me, I am first and foremost an honored citizen of Vienna, and I serve our great Emperor, lady!

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: And I thought you said this was a tolerant city ...

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: Oh yes, we are responsible for dealing with the problems caused by the arcanists, just as we deal with the Magyars and the Bohemians.
Mr. Karl swings his cane and strides forward cheerfully.

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: Alright, that's the venerable Vienna branch of the St. Pavlov Foundation over there. Let's go!
Marcus touches her left cheek, still warm from the touch of the mute incantation.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Mr. Karl is ... very different from the staff of the headquarters ...

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: In fact, most of the time the branch members aren't comrades who share the same goals with us. They're more like ... local officials we have to deal with.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: We need them as a buffer between the Foundation and the local governments. They can help us maintain peace in the human world.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: But you can't ask too much of them. Not all of them are cosmopolitans. Most of them put their Emperor and their country first.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: That's why we shouldn't disclose classified information to them.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: ... Does it still hurt?

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Um? It feels much better now!

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: Good.
The mentor swings around as if on a swivel, with a face of plain curiosity.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: ... Marcus, did you already have that license before you joined the Foundation?

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Yes. Austria abolished that policy in 1868, but Romania did not until 1913 ...

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: I carried it with me out of habit. Thank goodness I did.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: This is indeed the era I'm from ... That time has returned.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: Never disclose any information about the "Storm" or the "era" to irrelevant people.
The apprentice halts her speech, cowed by Hofmann's warning.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: Put away your license. We need to catch up with Karl.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: Remember my words, Marcus: never trust anyone, even if they're a branch member of the Foundation.
TO BE CONTINUED…
